notable_absence.finding: This page's Security section is the most specific about roles anywhere in the batch's admin/settings/query trio - it names two concrete roles (Full Admin, Cluster Admin) rather than the generic 'admin credentials' language on n1ql-rest-admin and n1ql-rest-query. But it still carries none of this round's other version-gating signals: no availableSince anywhere, and queryN1QLFeatCtrl repeats the exact same unexplained 'provided for technical support only' pattern already flagged as a gap on n1ql-rest-admin, this time at the cluster tier. Two settings (queryCleanupWindow, queryNumAtrs) name 'active transaction records' as what they configure, but in both cases the term is embedded inside a Markdown link to a different page's anchor, splitting what would otherwise be a clean, quotable defining sentence - the identical defect already flagged on n1ql-rest-admin for the same two settings, now confirmed independently at the cluster tier rather than fixed.

cross_component_finding:
This page is the cluster-level mirror of the near-duplicate-naming problem already flagged twice elsewhere in this batch (js-udf:library/js-udf:udf-library on n1ql-rest-functions): n1ql:curl-access-list (unpromoted, minted in round 10's intro.json purely from a link-table row reading '[Update CURL Access List](../../n1ql-rest-settings/index.md#post%5Faccess)') and n1ql:query-curl-whitelist (promoted, first minted from this feature's actual wire setting name queryCurlWhitelist) name the exact same Access object this page defines. The docs themselves use both names interchangeably in one page - the resource heading says 'curl Access List' (matching n1ql:curl-access-list's label) while the JSON wire format and the cluster-level settings table both say 'queryCurlWhitelist' / 'curlWhitelist' (matching n1ql:query-curl-whitelist's label) - so this is not an extraction error so much as the SOURCE material itself carrying two names for one thing, which the corpus then picked up as two separate ids. Reconciliation should fold n1ql:curl-access-list into n1ql:query-curl-whitelist, the same direction as the js-udf case.

Separately: n1ql:query-tmp-space-setting is this record's one first-contact mechanism, and it is the first place in the corpus (as far as this batch's checks could confirm) where a single setting is stated to be consumed by two DIFFERENT services (Index and Query) under two different names for the same kind of thing (backfill files vs spill files), with a THIRD service's mere co-deployment (Search/FTS) tripling the effective disk budget without Search itself configuring anything. This is a genuinely different shape from the settings-tier overrides (cluster/node/request) that dominate the rest of this batch: it is one resource shared by service co-deployment, not one setting expressed at multiple scopes.
cross_product_finding: Consistent with the rest of this batch: no Capella equivalent exists for this page. Capella has no exposed /settings/querySettings surface and no Cluster-Admin-role-gated cluster-wide Query configuration; cloud/n1ql/ documents only request-level parameters. The CURL() access list (queryCurlWhitelist / n1ql:curl-all-access etc.) is the one setting on this page most likely to have a genuine Capella analogue worth checking at reconciliation, since CURL()'s external-network-access risk is exactly the kind of thing a managed cloud service would need to control somehow even without exposing this specific cluster-level REST surface - but no page read in this round states what that Capella-side control is, so this is left as an open question rather than an asserted relation.
